en: The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon that brings dry weather to the Philippines between November and February.
Mayon Volcano in Albay is a highly active stratovolcano famous for its nearly perfect conical shape.
Romblon province is known as the Marble Capital of the Philippines because of its abundant marble deposits.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River is an eight-kilometer long subterranean waterway that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
The nutrient-rich volcanic soil surrounding Taal Volcano in Batangas allows local farmers to successfully cultivate coffee and pineapple crops.
Indigenous Filipino farmers watch for the Moroporo star cluster, locally known as the Pleiades, to signal the start of planting season.
The Valley Fault System is a major active fault line in Luzon that can trigger strong tectonic earthquakes.
PAGASA assigns local names to typhoons entering the Philippine Area of Responsibility to help citizens prepare for severe weather.
Surigao del Norte contains some of the largest nickel laterite deposits in the world, which are mined locally.
The moon's gravitational pull causes the daily tidal fluctuations that bring fish into the mangrove forests of Palawan.
The city of Baguio has a tropical highland climate, making it significantly cooler than the lowland city of Manila.
Intense solar radiation heating the warm waters of the Philippine Sea causes high evaporation rates that fuel afternoon thunderstorms.
